title: Newfoundland and Labrador Rebate Calculator 2026: Oil to Electric and takeCHARGE
h1: Newfoundland and Labrador Rebate Calculator 2026: What You Could Get Back
desc: Free Newfoundland and Labrador rebate calculator. Up to $22,000 to switch from oil to a heat pump, takeCHARGE insulation, air sealing and HRV rebates, with the official source for every amount.
intro: Answer a few questions and see which Newfoundland and Labrador rebates fit your home, with a source for every number.
short: Homes heated with oil or propane can get up to $22,000 to switch to a central heat pump through the Oil to Electric program if their income qualifies, or up to $9,000 if not. Homes already on electric heat can get takeCHARGE rebates of up to $3,000 for insulation and up to $750 for air sealing. Lower-income homes can apply for no-cost upgrades.
faq: How much can I get to switch from oil to a heat pump in Newfoundland?

Up to $22,000 for a central heat pump if your household is income-qualified, or up to $9,000 if not. A multi-split or several mini-splits get up to $18,000 or $6,500, and an electric furnace or boiler up to $10,000 or $5,000.
Is there a heat pump rebate if my home already has electric heat?

We found no takeCHARGE heat pump rebate for homes already heated by electricity. Newfoundland Power and NL Hydro offer on-bill financing for heat pumps instead, and lower-income homes can apply to the TakeCharge Greener Homes Program.
Who qualifies for the takeCHARGE insulation rebate?

Homeowners whose main heat is electric, in homes built and connected before January 1, 2014. It pays 75% of the insulation cost up to $1,000 each for the attic and basement, plus up to $500 each for labour.
Is there a solar or battery rebate in Newfoundland and Labrador?
We found no takeCHARGE solar or battery rebate for homeowners.

programs.name: takeCHARGE insulation rebate
programs.rules: 75% of cost up to $1,000 attic and $1,000 basement, plus up to $500 labour each with a participating installer. Main heat must be electric; home built before 2014.

programs.name: takeCHARGE air sealing rebate
programs.rules: $200 to $750 based on blower door results. Main heat must be electric and the home needs an HRV or air exchanger.

programs.name: takeCHARGE HRV rebate
programs.rules: Eligible high-efficiency model installed by an HRAI certified installer. Any heat source. Paid as a bill credit.

programs.name: TakeCharge Greener Homes Program (no-cost upgrades)
programs.rules: Income-qualified homeowners. A limited number of no-cost heat pumps, HRVs, insulation and air sealing upgrades after a home energy assessment.

programs.name: Home Heating Supplement (oil)
programs.rules: Provincial payment for people who bought at least 250 litres of furnace or stove oil in 2026, with 2025 family income of $150,000 or less. Apply by January 15, 2027. Not an upgrade rebate, so it is not added to your total.

programs.name: National Heat Pump Rebate (federal, not open yet)
programs.rules: Announced October 8, 2026 and expected to launch in early 2027. The income line, eligible homes and how it combines with provincial programs are not published, so this is shown but not added to your total.

notes: We found no takeCHARGE heat pump rebate for homes already on electric heat, and no homeowner solar or battery rebate.
Amounts are the most a program pays. Your rebate depends on your quote and final invoice.
